long_biography.plain_text:
Artal linked Eric Wittouck's inherited industrial stake to his later investment fortune. His grandfather Paul and great-uncle Franz acquired the Tiense refinery in 1894. After Wittouck inherited an interest, he and cousins controlled the producer during the 1980s. Its 1989 transfer to Südzucker released capital for a different ownership model. The transaction price covered the business collectively, not his individual payout.

Those proceeds financed positions across consumer, food and growth companies. Wittouck subsequently bought his relatives' Artal interests and kept the capital with Invus, a manager pursuing long-duration private and public investments. The retained pool produced major gains under professional allocation. Invus's assets-under-management figure belongs to that platform; each portfolio company also keeps its own assets and valuation. Current securities filings place Amaury Wittouck at the head of the top holding foundation. Eric is therefore best understood as the investor whose capital underpins the structure, rather than its present daily manager.
